Cs101 gdb 

*My Selected Option: Option 1 - Unintentional / Careless Mistakes*

I agree with the IT Manager. In my opinion, careless mistakes are more dangerous and harder to manage than intentional attacks.

The main reason is that every employee can make a mistake. A malicious employee is only one person, but carelessness can happen with 100 employees every day. For example, an employee may use a weak password like "12345", click on a fake email link, or by mistake send a confidential file to the wrong person on WhatsApp or email.

Second, these mistakes are very hard to detect because there is no bad intention. No one tries to hide anything, so the company does not even know that data is leaked until it is too late.

A malicious attack can be stopped by strict access control and monitoring, but human error cannot be fully stopped by technology. It can only be reduced by regular training and awareness. That is why unintentional mistakes pose the greater threat to a company.

*CS101 – GDB SOLUTION BY mano*

*Option 2: Intentional/Malicious Actions pose the greater threat*

In my opinion option 2 is more dangerous. Careless mistakes happen quite often but they are usually unintentional and can sometimes be fixed quickly. For example if an employee accidentally sends a private file to the wrong person the IT team can take action before things get worse.

A malicious employee is a different kind of threat. They already have access to company systems because the company trusts them. Instead of hacking anything they can misuse their existing access. The difficult part is that they may try to hide their activities so nobody notices. For example an unhappy employee who is about to leave the company might secretly copy customer records or important business information and share it with a competitor.

Careless mistakes are usually unplanned but malicious actions can involve proper planning and a clear intention to cause harm. This makes them harder to detect and control.

So I believe mistakes may be more common but intentional actions can cause greater damage and are much harder for a company to manage.
